questions.prompt: State what happens when the like poles of two magnets are brought together.
questions.answer: They repel.

questions.prompt: State the difference between a permanent magnet and an induced magnet.
questions.answer: A permanent magnet produces its own magnetic field; an induced magnet only becomes magnetic when placed in a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: State what happens to an induced magnet when it is removed from the magnetic field.
questions.answer: It loses most or all of its magnetism quickly.

questions.prompt: Define the poles of a magnet.
questions.answer: The places on a magnet where the magnetic forces are strongest.

questions.prompt: Define an induced magnet.
questions.answer: A material that becomes a magnet when it is placed in a magnetic field.

questions.prompt: State the type of force that induced magnetism always causes.
questions.answer: A force of attraction.

questions.prompt: State the direction of a magnetic field line outside a bar magnet.
questions.answer: From the north pole to the south pole.

questions.prompt: State where the magnetic field of a bar magnet is strongest.
questions.answer: At its poles.

questions.prompt: State what a compass needle's behaviour suggests about the Earth's core.
questions.answer: The Earth's core must be magnetic, since the compass needle points along the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.prompt: Define a magnetic field.
questions.answer: The region around a magnet where a force acts on another magnet or on a magnetic material.

questions.prompt: Name the four magnetic materials.
questions.answer: Iron, steel, cobalt and nickel.

questions.prompt: State how the direction of a magnetic field at a point is defined.
questions.answer: The direction of the force that would act on another north pole placed at that point.

questions.prompt: State what surrounds a wire when a current flows through it.
questions.answer: A magnetic field.

questions.prompt: State the shape of wire that concentrates the magnetic field of a current into a strong, uniform field inside the coil.
questions.answer: A solenoid (coil).

questions.prompt: State what an electromagnet is.
questions.answer: A solenoid with an iron core.

questions.prompt: State two factors that affect the strength of the magnetic field around a straight wire carrying a current.
questions.answer: The current through the wire and the distance from the wire.

questions.prompt: State the effect of adding an iron core to a solenoid.
questions.answer: It increases the strength of the magnetic field.

title: Force on a conductor and Fleming's left-hand rule

questions.prompt: Name the rule that shows the relative directions of force, current and magnetic field.
questions.answer: Fleming's left-hand rule.

questions.prompt: State the name of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.
questions.answer: The motor effect.

questions.prompt: Define the motor effect.
questions.answer: When a conductor carrying a current is placed in a magnetic field, the magnet producing the field and the conductor exert a force on each other.

questions.prompt: State the factors that affect the size of the force on a conductor carrying a current at right angles to a magnetic field.
questions.answer: The magnetic flux density, the current and the length of the conductor in the field.

questions.prompt: State what a coil of wire carrying a current in a magnetic field tends to do.
questions.answer: Rotate.

questions.prompt: State the unit of magnetic flux density.
questions.answer: The tesla (T).

questions.prompt: State what a loudspeaker converts variations in current into.
questions.answer: Pressure variations in sound waves (using the motor effect).

questions.prompt: Name the effect in which a conductor moving through a magnetic field induces a potential difference.
questions.answer: The generator effect.

questions.prompt: State what an induced current does to the change that causes it.
questions.answer: It generates a magnetic field that opposes the original change.

questions.prompt: State the condition for an induced potential difference to produce a current.
questions.answer: The conductor must be part of a complete circuit.

questions.prompt: Define the generator effect.
questions.answer: If a conductor moves relative to a magnetic field, or the magnetic field around it changes, a potential difference is induced across the ends of the conductor (and a current if it is part of a complete circuit).

questions.prompt: State the type of current an alternator generates.
questions.answer: Alternating current (ac).

questions.prompt: State the type of current a dynamo generates.
questions.answer: Direct current (dc).

questions.prompt: State the effect a moving-coil microphone uses to convert sound waves into variations in current.
questions.answer: The generator effect.

questions.prompt: State what a basic transformer consists of.
questions.answer: A primary coil and a secondary coil wound on an iron core.

questions.prompt: State why iron is used as the core of a transformer.
questions.answer: It is easily magnetised.

questions.prompt: State whether the secondary potential difference is greater or less than the primary potential difference in a step-up transformer.
questions.answer: Greater (Vs > Vp).

questions.prompt: State whether the secondary potential difference is greater or less than the primary potential difference in a step-down transformer.
questions.answer: Less (Vs < Vp).

questions.prompt: State how the electrical power output compares with the power input for a 100% efficient transformer.
questions.answer: They are equal (Vs × Is = Vp × Ip).

questions.prompt: Calculate the secondary potential difference of a transformer with 100 primary turns, 1000 secondary turns and a 230 V primary potential difference.
